geometry_edits.rationale: Swap the split-wing macro for a courtyard macro to produce one dominant mass with a carved public void and clearer access-side response.
Create a substantial but bounded court rather than a decorative notch.
Open the court toward the verified program access side to restore an active street threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the split-wing/cantilever logic with a more legible public court response to the frontage so the dominant mass becomes one continuous neighborhood bar around a void.
Open a usable court rather than a narrow abstract cut; strengthen public void and ground threshold.
Align the void to the program-frame access side so the frontage edge can read as a public entry court.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent bent/split mass in some views, but the four-view set also shows a strong mismatch between views: in plan and opposite view it fragments into multiple wedge-like pieces, and the section/silhouette does not convincingly resolve into a single occupiable neighborhood-living volume. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly; the ground response is more of a central cut-through than a clear public threshold aligned to access. The parcel is respected, but the form feels more like an abstract stepped/angled object than a compact mixed-use street building with active edge, public void, and calm upper hierarchy. Because the visible mass does not reliably establish a legible neighborhood program section, program_fit_hard_pass fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus/community-center than compact street-edge housing; use the courtyard/terrace principle, not the dispersed campus scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise clustered massing with a meaningful central void and connected wing logic can support neighborhood living.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Single-story hospitality pavilion is much simpler and flatter than this candidate; do not copy the roof language or assume a tower-like add-on.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A calm low-rise bar with a clear entry cut and canopy-like ground response can support active frontage.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is a large residential waterfront complex; the candidate should borrow the sectional-public-space idea only, not the expansive scale or long continuous slab.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/terraced section can create inhabited outdoor space and a strong public-facing ground edge.

warnings: Coherence is view-dependent; the form reads better in perspective than in plan and front.
Frontage response is present but not strongly legible as an access-aligned public threshold.
The silhouette trends toward an abstract stepped object rather than a neighborhood-living massing typology.
